papers.title_en: Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Can Be Strong and Efficient Retrievers
papers.authors: Anubhav Shrestha, Safal Shrestha, Minwu Kim, Torsten Suel, Keith Ross
papers.evidence: MoE大模型用于高效推理与降低编码成本
papers.tldr: 密集LLM检索器效果随规模提升，但查询与文档都需过全模型，编码成本随参数量增长。本文系统训练同流程的MoE与密集LLM检索器，跨数据集评测并测同服务配置下的查询编码时间。MoE检索器在相近激活参数量下优于密集模型最多3.0 nDCG@10；最强MoE以少59%激活参数、低18%查询时间匹配8B密集检索器。减少查询编码专家数无需重训或重建索引，保留超99%效果并最多降26%查询时间，表明MoE可作强且高效的一阶段检索器。
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has shown that fine-tuning decoder-only large language models (LLMs) for retrieval yields strong first-stage retrievers, with effectiveness improving as backbones grow in size. However, every query and document must pass through the full model, so encoding cost increases with model size. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs activate only a subset of parameters per token and are widely used to scale generative models, yet remain underexplored as retrievers. We systematically study MoE backbones for retrieval by training MoE and dense LLMs from several families using the same procedure, evaluating them across diverse datasets, and measuring query encoding time under the same serving configuration. We show that MoE retrievers outperform dense retrievers with comparable active parameter counts by up to 3.0 nDCG@10 points on BEIR. One of our strongest MoE retrievers matches an 8B dense retriever with 59% fewer active parameters and 18% lower query encoding time. We further show that the number of experts used for query encoding can be reduced without retraining or re-indexing, retaining more than 99% of retrieval effectiveness while reducing query encoding time by up to 26%. Recent rerankers provide only modest additional gains over strong MoE first stages, which often match or exceed the reranked configurations we evaluate. Together, these results show that MoE LLMs can be strong and efficient first-stage retrievers.
